clauses.title: 2.1 Irreversible actions (shutdown/reboot, disk format, recursive delete, registry writes, download-and-execute) require explicit per-turn user authorization.
2.2 Before any irreversible action, state the rollback path and what cannot be recovered.
2.3 Payloads of write/exec tools pass the L3 output guard. A blocked payload is hard-stopped (an exception), not merely suggested.
2.4 An unregistered tool name is denied by the PreToolUse adapter before it ever reaches the host.
2.5 An audited, one-time escape token may override a block only after the user explicitly authorizes that single call; the token is consumed on use.
